classes.name: Alpha-1 blockers
classes.description: Alpha-1 blockers for BPH: tamsulosin (Flomax), alfuzosin ER (Uroxatral), silodosin (Rapaflo), doxazosin (Cardura; Cardura XL is brand-only), terazosin. Combination dutasteride/tamsulosin (Jalyn) belongs to the 5-ARI class.
classes.plainDescription: A daily pill that relaxes the prostate so urine flows more easily.

classes.name: 5-alpha reductase inhibitors
classes.description: 5-alpha reductase inhibitors for BPH: finasteride 5 mg (Proscar), dutasteride (Avodart), dutasteride/tamsulosin (Jalyn), finasteride/tadalafil (Entadfi; up to 26 weeks, not with alpha blockers). The pick is a single agent; the combinations are alternatives. Finasteride 1 mg (Propecia, hair loss) is not this class.
classes.plainDescription: A daily pill that slowly shrinks an enlarged prostate over months.

classes.name: Tadalafil for BPH
classes.description: Tadalafil 2.5 mg and 5 mg once daily (Cialis, generic) for BPH symptoms. Plans often cover it for BPH only with a diagnosis-based PA and exclude it for erectile dysfunction: record the BPH rule. Sildenafil and vardenafil are not labeled for BPH.
classes.plainDescription: A low daily dose of tadalafil that eases urinary symptoms of an enlarged prostate.
